title: Asset Interest
description: Captures expressions of interest about an asset, collection, or product from any perspective — owner wishlists, beneficiary preferences, executor observations, proxy-relayed interests, and cross-system collector interest. Qualified by expressedByRole (who), intentType (what kind), and optionally productMatch (product-level vs asset-level). Maps to Schema.org ReactAction + Role

id.description: Unique identifier for this interest record

rootDocumentId.description: The root document this entity belongs to — either an estate document (schema.json) or a catalogue document (catalogue.json)

assetId.description: Reference to a specific Asset.id, if the interest is in a single asset

collectionId.description: Reference to an AssetCollection.id, if the interest is in an entire collection

personId.description: The person expressing interest (a Person.id). The person's relationship to the estate is qualified by expressedByRole

personIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced person

interestLevel.description: How strongly the beneficiary has expressed interest
interestLevel.$comment: mentioned = came up in conversation but no strong feeling. expressed_interest = person said they'd like it. strongly_wants = person has made it clear this matters to them. agreed = testator and beneficiary have informally agreed. When expressedByRole is 'testator', the levels carry directive weight: mentioned = noted as a possibility, expressed_interest = prefers this, strongly_wants = is clear about this, agreed = both parties have discussed and agreed.

sourceType.description: How this interest was communicated or recorded
sourceType.$comment: family_conversation = mentioned during a family discussion. written_request = beneficiary put it in writing. chat_message = expressed via the platform's messaging (generic). platform_private_message = private 1-to-1 message on the platform. platform_group_message = group message involving multiple parties. proxy_reported = a proxy relayed the interest on behalf of the beneficiary. testator_observed = testator noticed the person's attachment without them asking. manual = entered directly by the testator or proxy.

testatorAcknowledged.description: Whether the testator has seen and acknowledged this interest

examples: Sarah mentioned at Christmas 2024 that she'd love Mum's engagement ring. Mum seemed pleased.
Haruki has always admired the woodblock print collection — discussed at Obon 2024.
Amara expressed strong interest in the family compound during the last family council meeting.

organisationId.description: Reference to the Organisation.id expressing interest, if an organisation rather than a person. Mutually exclusive with personId

organisationIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced organisation

expressedByRole.description: The role of the person expressing this interest in relation to the estate or catalogue. Qualifies the authority and weight of the expression. Follows the Schema.org Role pattern
expressedByRole.$comment: testator = the estate/catalogue owner expressing a desire (directive weight). beneficiary = a named beneficiary expressing a preference. executor = an executor recording an observation or recommendation. proxy = relaying interest on behalf of another person. Extension values (x-inherit-) support additional roles such as collector interest from external systems.

intentType.description: The nature of the interest being expressed. Distinguishes between wanting to acquire, wanting to receive, wanting to allocate to someone, willingness to sell, and soft admiration
intentType.$comment: acquire = wants to buy or obtain (collector wishlist, shopping list). receive = would like to be given or inherit (beneficiary preference). allocate = wants to give this to a specific person (testator directive). sell = willing to part with this item (signals availability). admire = appreciates the item, no action intended (soft signal).

productMatch.description: Interest in any asset matching this product identity, rather than a specific asset. Use instead of assetId when the interest is in a product class, not a specific instance. Maps to Schema.org Product (vs IndividualProduct for assetId). Matching is by identifier (strongest), brand + category (medium), or category alone (weakest)

identifierValue.description: The product identifier value within the system

brandWikidataId.description: Wikidata entity ID for the brand — strongest cross-system brand match

category.description: INHERIT product category for broad matching

minimumCondition.description: Minimum acceptable condition. If absent, matches all conditions. Uses the same enum as asset.condition

notes.description: Additional matching criteria in free text

quantity.description: Number of items desired (for productMatch wishlist entries) or number of the specific asset being discussed. Default 1 if absent. Follows the same convention as asset.quantity

expressedAt.description: When this interest was expressed or recorded

preOrderStatus.description: For wishlist items that have been pre-ordered from a dealer or manufacturer but not yet received. Tracks order status, payment, and expected delivery

orderedFrom.description: The dealer or manufacturer the item was ordered from

orderReference.description: The dealer's or manufacturer's order reference number

expectedDeliveryDate.description: When the item is expected to arrive. Manufacturers often announce target quarters rather than exact dates

paymentStatus.description: Whether the item has been paid for

amountPaid.description: The amount paid so far, in minor currency units

provenance.description: Consolidated provenance metadata — how this entity was created, by whom, and whether a human has verified it
